intro: This course covered why accurate records matter, the principles of good documentation, and the data protection law that governs how you record care.
points: CQC Regulation 17 requires accurate, complete and contemporaneous records; write at or close to the time, never days later from memory.
Never falsify or backdate records and never sign for care you did not give — your login and signature mean you did it.
Record facts, not opinions or assumptions — write only what you saw, heard or did, in respectful, person-centred language.
Keep records secure under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018; never share your login, and report breaches promptly.
Correct a paper error with a single crossing line, initials and date; never erase, scribble out or use correction fluid.
People can ask to see records about them; pass any subject access request to your manager, who must respond within one month.
